_comment: Long-form project copy for projects/<slug>.html. Read by tools/generate-seo.mjs. Slugs match the generated pages. Keep it free of em dashes, hype and programming-language names, in line with the rest of the site.

overview: A multi-tenant retail platform for small traders, built for how trade actually happens: a counter sale, a market run, a customer who sends a list and pays on delivery. It ships as a backend service, a web application and an offline-first mobile client.

The engineering spine is a five-layer architecture with enforced import contracts: entities, schemas, persistence, services and transport. No outward imports, no logic in transport, no database driver outside the persistence boundary, and the build fails on a violation rather than a reviewer catching it.
highlights: Every business-owned table carries a row-level security policy bound into the transaction, so a query that forgets its tenant filter returns nothing rather than another shop's data. A missing scope fails closed.

Sales, payments, stock movements, expenses, audit events and the ledger are append-only and committed together, so a failure part-way through cannot leave half-recorded money. The rule is enforced by database triggers, not by convention.

Money is never floating point. A price arriving as a float is refused rather than rounded, prices carry at most two decimal places, and they travel the wire as decimal strings so no client passes money through a binary float.

Offline devices queue operations under a stable operation identifier and push them through a sync service, so a retry after a lost reply cannot book the same sale twice. Inventory merges additively, catalogue edits resolve last-writer-wins, and a customer draft conflict is surfaced rather than silently resolved.

Authorization is data. Atomic permissions compose into permission sets and then roles, resolved deny-by-default, and a caller cannot grant a permission they do not hold. The interface hides what a role cannot do instead of offering a button that fails.

The catalogue is an arbitrarily deep category tree with price inheritance, so a grade carries one price and only the exceptions are listed by name. A customer can add an item the shop has never stocked, leaving the price for the trader to set.

A customer builds a list from a public link without an account and is remembered by phone number. The list is shared as a generated image or a multi-page PDF, because a typed list arrives truncated on a phone and cannot be forwarded as a list.
Dispatch records the transporter, the waybill number, the trip cost and a tracking link, so a parcel on a road is attributable and the cost of the run comes off what the list made.
Storage and media sit behind a provider-neutral port with two interchangeable adapters, server-side validation and optimisation, and per-tenant quota accounting that holds under concurrent uploads.
Deployment is one push: the image is built in CI and addressed by commit, a migration job runs before traffic moves, and a rollback is a pointer at an earlier tag rather than a rebuild.
Roughly two thousand tests, including architecture contracts, an ASCII guard, secret scanning and a dependency audit gate that fails the build on a critical finding.

overview: A retrieval-augmented generation framework published on PyPI, built around one idea: getting from a document to a live streaming question-answering API should take a single command.

Point the CLI at a source-of-truth document, hand it a system prompt, and it loads, chunks, indexes and serves a FastAPI endpoint with token-by-token server-sent events and per-session conversation memory.
highlights: Six vector stores and two retrievers are chosen by configuration, or replaced entirely with your own classes through an import path, without forking the package.
Any hosted or local model provider can be swapped with one flag, with automatic fallback to a backup model when one is unavailable.
Rolling conversation memory compresses history into running summaries, so context stays bounded across a long session.
Marker-aware buffering stops partially formed markup from reaching the client mid-stream.
The same pipeline is available as a programmatic API and as a one-shot CLI query when a server is not needed.

overview: A hyper-local services marketplace for Nigerian university towns and residential communities, where the tradespeople people actually need (electricians, plumbers, welders, tailors) are found today by asking around. It replaces that with a verifiable local directory, an escrow contract and a reputation that cannot be discarded.

The design problem is leakage: the first transaction tends to leave the platform. GigR answers it structurally rather than by policy. A client stays because the money is held until the finished work is inspected. A tradesperson stays because a vouch is only minted by a settled escrow transaction, so taking the deal off-platform costs them the credential they need to win the next, better-paying client.
highlights: Four failure points it is built against: requests that go unanswered during a night-time emergency, verbal referrals with no record of past work, advance payments of half to four-fifths of a job with no recourse, and an identity that consists of a phone number somebody can simply block.

Discovery evaluates physical distance directly instead of administrative boundaries, with graduated 5, 10, 25 and 50 kilometre search radii and exact proximity shown per listing. A provider registers from live device coordinates or drops a pin on a fixed workshop.
A single profile holds symmetric rights: the same account can post a job and publish a service listing, so a user can offer electrical work while hiring a chef.
Escrow releases on confirmed completion, with milestone tranches for work delivered in stages. A provider who never accepts an assigned task has the deposit returned automatically by timeout.

Reputation is minted as compressed tokens at the moment escrow settles, using Merkle summaries to keep on-chain storage in fractions of a kobo. A vouch cannot exist without economic value having moved, which removes fake reviews rather than policing them.

Disputes route to a community courtroom instead of central moderation. The evidence bundle (contract room messages, agreed terms, photographic proof) goes to platform users on jury duty, and a majority decides whether funds go to the worker, back to the client, or split proportionally.

An assistant called GigidyAI takes spoken commands through one global microphone button and extracts intent, category, radius and price constraints from plain speech. A deterministic parser takes over when the model is slow or unreachable, so the feature degrades rather than disappearing.

Agent autonomy is a setting the user owns: off, auto-reply, auto-negotiation, auto-apply, or full autonomous job hunting, with a server-enforced ceiling of twenty autonomous operations per account per day so nothing runs away at scale.
The agent can also place an outbound telephone call with a spoken summary when it finds a match, which means an alert does not require somebody to be looking at a screen.

overview: A simulation research platform that asks whether multi-agent reinforcement learning can learn better TCP congestion control than the established algorithms.
The work runs entirely inside ns-3 rather than modifying a live kernel, so every experiment starts from an identical controlled environment and an untrained policy cannot damage a real network.
highlights: Agents learn to trade throughput against fairness per flow instead of applying one fixed loss-based rule.
Behaviour is measured against the mainstream congestion control algorithms under the same conditions.
Simulation traces are captured with netanim, so a result can be watched rather than only read as a number.
Reproducibility is the point of the simulator choice: any experiment can be re-run and compared.

overview: A commit-time gatekeeper that stops documentation from drifting away from the code it describes. It watches what a commit actually changes, detects when a structural change is not reflected in the Markdown docs, and either blocks the commit or rewrites the affected documentation to match.
Stale documentation becomes a build failure rather than a promise to fix it later.
highlights: Detects structural change, including function signatures, class methods and exported types, rather than comparing prose.
Ships three ways: a standalone CLI, a pre-commit hook, and a GitHub Action, so the check follows the workflow a team already has.
Can anchor each documentation-sync check to Solana, producing an immutable record that the docs matched the code at the moment of a commit.
Version 0.4.0 is the current release, and the walkthrough is on YouTube.

overview: An autonomous trading system where agents manage a Solana treasury through a multi-agent consensus loop, built for the Agentic Wallets challenge run by Superteam Nigeria.
Four agents run in sequence on a fixed interval: one reads live market data, one proposes a trade, one grades the proposal, and one signs and submits it.
highlights: A proposal has to clear three independent gates before anything reaches the chain: hard limits that no model can override, deterministic policy checks, and a second model acting as an independent reviewer.
The reviewer is a separate agent from the proposer, so a single bad generation cannot approve itself.
An adversarial test suite verifies the guardrails hold when the proposing agent is actively trying to defeat them.
Real chain, real market data, no simulated balances in the execution path.

overview: A freelance marketplace and reputation-weighted governance platform built to price trust cryptographically instead of trusting a profile that nobody verified.
Job access and voting power are both gated on an on-chain reputation score, so a new wallet cannot buy its way into governance on day one.
highlights: Clients can require a minimum reputation score for a listing, which makes the gate enforceable rather than advisory.
Escrow backs the contract between both sides, so payment and delivery are linked.
Governance weight follows reputation, so influence has to be earned through completed work.
Full-stack, deployed, and built with mobile use in mind.

overview: An agentic intent solver for the Injective ecosystem with hardware-enforced execution, built as a bounty submission. The design separates intelligence from execution on principle: the part that reasons holds no keys.

The intelligence layer reads live chain state, watches pending staking rewards and constructs the payload, then hands it to a Ledger device where a person reviews and clear-signs before anything is broadcast.
highlights: Zero private keys in the agent process, so a compromised model cannot move funds on its own.
Human approval happens on the hardware device rather than in the application, which is the difference between a prompt and a guarantee.
Includes a staking auto-compounder that withdraws and re-delegates rewards, and a buy-back trigger that constructs a commitment payload.
Built against the Injective MCP servers for live chain queries.

overview: A multi-tenant backend for healthcare organisations such as hospitals, clinics and diagnostic laboratories, covering patient records, test requests and results.
The standout piece is the permission model, which borrows its shape from AWS IAM: atomic permissions compose into permission sets, and permission sets compose into roles.
highlights: Tenant isolation between facilities is structural rather than a convention, so a clinic cannot reach another clinic's records.
Authorization is data rather than hardcoded checks, so a facility can define what a role means without a code change.
Records use soft deletes, which keeps an auditable history instead of destroying it.
Credentials are hashed with Argon2.

overview: A legal assistant that answers questions about the Nigerian Constitution, aimed at people who need an answer and do not have a lawyer to hand.
Retrieval is hybrid on purpose: vector search over embeddings is paired with keyword scoring, so exact statutory phrasing and paraphrased questions both find the right passage.
highlights: Hybrid FAISS and BM25 retrieval, because statute text is full of precise phrases that pure vector search blurs.
Answers are grounded in retrieved passages rather than generated from memory.
Built to run on modest hosting, so the cost of answering a question stays close to zero.

overview: A patient management system split into independent services for patients, authentication, appointments, billing and analytics.
Services communicate over Kafka events where the work is asynchronous, REST where a request needs a reply, and gRPC for the calls that need to be fast and typed.
highlights: The environment is provisioned with AWS CDK against LocalStack, so the cloud topology can be brought up and torn down locally.
Redis backs caching and rate limiting across services.
Observability runs through Prometheus, Grafana and service health endpoints.
Container images are built in multiple stages, so the runtime image carries only what it needs.

overview: An analytics platform for the African creator economy. It aggregates cross-platform metrics into an influence score, then exposes creator discovery and campaign planning to the agencies and brands doing the hiring.
The first integration is YouTube analytics, covering engagement, reach and audience demographics.
highlights: Influence scoring is heuristic and documented, so a ranking can be explained rather than asserted.
A normalisation layer sits between the platforms, so adding a source does not change the scoring code.
Authentication uses short-lived sessions in HTTP-only cookies.
Built as a typed API with a separate front end.

overview: A retrieval agent built on the kssrag framework, written to exercise the published package in real use rather than in a test harness.
It rewrites a question before searching and declines to answer when the retrieved context does not support one.
highlights: Serves as the working proof that the packaged framework behaves the same way when installed from the index.
Carries a rejection path, which matters more than the answering path for a retrieval system.

overview: A live demonstration that runs in this page. A model loads in the browser and detects objects through the webcam, with no server involved.
Classification and the confidence threshold are applied client side, and no frame leaves the device.
highlights: Runs entirely in the browser, so there is no round trip per frame and nothing to upload.
Individual object classes can be filtered out, which is what makes the output readable on a busy image.
The confidence threshold is adjustable while the camera is running.

overview: A prescription processing system for pharmacies. A photograph of a prescription goes in; structured, validated medication data comes out.
Optical character recognition extracts the raw text, and a language model structures it into fields and corrects what recognition got wrong, which is the failure mode that matters on handwriting.
highlights: Multi-tenant inventory, so separate pharmacies keep separate stock.
Demand forecasting on top of dispensing history, aimed at ordering rather than reporting.
Validation sits between recognition and storage, so a misread does not silently become a record.

overview: The first version of the retrieval agent, kept for reference. It answers questions about skills, database usage, deployment platforms and background from an indexed corpus.
Superseded by the second version, which was rebuilt on the packaged framework.
highlights: Chunking for large documents so context stays within the window.
Session-based conversation, so follow-up questions have something to refer to.
Kept as the record of how the approach developed.

overview: A service that turns a vague ambition into a structured specification. A person describes what they want to build, and the agent runs a scoping dialogue that narrows it into goals, feasibility and a challenge definition.
It loads platform-specific schemas dynamically, so the same agent can produce a definition for a different platform without a code change.
highlights: Model output is constrained to a schema the API validates before it is stored.
Retrieval over similar past challenges informs the questions it asks.
The scoping dialogue adapts to earlier answers rather than following a fixed script.

overview: A Telegram bot that reports Solana on-chain activity using the Vybe Network APIs. Wallet balances, token prices, whale movements and charts, in a conversation.
Replies are shaped for a phone screen, because that is where the question is being asked.
highlights: Wallet balance lookup for any Solana address.
Price charts over selectable timeframes.
Whale and activity monitoring delivered as a message rather than a dashboard.

overview: A Telegram bot that analyses a token's holder structure using Bubblemaps data, renders the bubble map, and reports concentration risk.
The point is to answer whether a small number of wallets control a token, without the user opening a block explorer.
highlights: Holder cluster analysis, so connected wallets are treated as one position.
Risk assessment reported alongside the map rather than left to interpretation.
Written up as a case study alongside the code.

overview: A published dataset joining air quality against avoidable mortality across 100 UK local authorities for 2022.
The two series come from different sources with different geographic conventions, so the work is in making them directly comparable at authority level.
highlights: Published and downloadable on Kaggle.
Built for environmental health analysis rather than as a demonstration.
Documents the join so the result can be reproduced or challenged.

overview: A data preparation pipeline for the Home Credit default risk problem, turning seven raw relational tables into six domain-specific datasets built for modelling.
Most of the work is in the transformation: relational history becomes behaviour a model can actually use.
highlights: Feature engineering driven by what the data means for credit risk rather than by what is easy to compute.
Memory footprint reduced substantially without discarding information.
Behavioural signals derived from mobile usage and application history.

overview: A retrieval system built over scraped drug monographs. Ask about an interaction or a dosage and it answers from the source text rather than from model memory.
The scraper had to move from simple requests to a full browser engine, because the source renders content after load and a plain fetch returns an empty shell.
highlights: Answers cite the passage they came from, which is the only defensible way to answer a medical question.
Handles the awkward parts of the source, including dosage tables that do not follow the page's usual structure.
The companion scraper produces the corpus this system reads.

overview: A scraper that walks every condition page on ada.com and extracts each section heading together with the content beneath it, covering symptoms, causes and types.
The extraction follows the page's own structure: headings mark the boundaries, and the blocks between them are the content.
highlights: Outputs JSON and CSV, so the result is usable for analysis and for medical language processing.
Structure is preserved rather than flattened, so a symptom stays attached to its condition.
Built as source material for retrieval and modelling work.

overview: The scraper that produces the drug corpus: monographs from drugs.com, extracted into structured JSON.
Intended as source material for retrieval and interaction modelling rather than as a finished product.
highlights: Structured output keyed for downstream retrieval.
Handles the pagination and lazy loading of the source.
Companion to the retrieval system built on top of it.

overview: An animated single-page pitch deck for Gigr, written in plain browser modules with Three.js and no framework or bundler.
Nine full-screen slides run on a step-based reveal engine over a live 3D background, with bloom post-processing and transitions that behave the same going forwards and backwards.
highlights: Navigation loops, so the deck can be driven with a clicker without hitting a dead end.
Content reveals a step at a time, which keeps attention on the point being made.
Keyboard, scroll, swipe and click all drive the same state machine.
No build step: the repository is the deployed artefact.

overview: A platform for competitive FPS players entering real-world events, covering registration, brackets and scheduling in one place.
Built for events that happen in a room rather than online, so the schedule is the part people actually depend on.
highlights: Team and player registration for an event.
Bracket and match scheduling.
Deployed and usable from a phone on event day.

overview: The chat backend behind the assistant on this site. It runs a locally hosted model by default, and falls back to a hosted provider when the local path is unavailable.
Keeping a local path first means the common case does not depend on someone else's uptime.
highlights: Local model by default, hosted provider as fallback.
Session handling so a conversation has continuity.
Streams replies rather than waiting for a complete answer.

overview: A REST API for acquisitions and authentication, built with sessions in HTTP-only cookies and role-based access control.
Security is treated as the feature rather than an afterthought: rate limiting and bot defence at the edge, strict input validation, and security headers on every response.
highlights: Role-based access control across user and administrator actions.
Typed database access with migrations rather than ad-hoc queries.
Rate limiting and bot protection in front of the API.
Interactive API documentation kept alongside the code.

overview: A Telegram bot that gathers several small utilities behind one command interface, so a single conversation handles several unrelated jobs.
The value is convenience: one place to reach for instead of four.
highlights: A single command surface over several independent tools.
Built to stay within the free tier of the messaging platform.

overview: A portfolio site delivered for a biochemistry researcher, covering publications, current research and a media gallery.
Built so the owner can update it without touching markup, which for an academic is the difference between a site that stays current and one that does not.
highlights: Publications and research presented as the primary content rather than an afterthought.
Media gallery for lab and fieldwork images.
Content is editable without a developer.

overview: Two halves of one platform for a content creator: a public editorial site, and a private dashboard that lets the owner rewrite copy, change colours, upload media and reorder work without touching code.
The requirement was concrete. The person using it does not write code, so every piece of content and presentation had to be reachable from the dashboard.
highlights: A public site designed to read as editorial rather than as a template.
A private dashboard covering copy, palette, media and ordering.
Media hosted on a delivery network with server-side upload handling.
Runs entirely on free tiers of the hosting, database and media services.

overview: A shared drawing canvas where several people paint on the same board at the same time.
Built to explore real-time state synchronisation: what happens when two people draw in the same place at the same instant.
highlights: Multiple concurrent clients on one canvas.
Realtime updates rather than a refresh to see someone else's strokes.

overview: A price board for crypto assets with sorting by price and by recent momentum, reading from a public market data API.
The interesting part is the sort: ranking by change rather than by market cap changes what the list is actually telling you.
highlights: Sorting by price and by momentum.
Live data from a public market API.
Runs without a backend.

overview: A weather lookup by city, with current conditions and a short forecast.
Built as a small, focused piece of interface rather than a dashboard.
highlights: Search by city name.
Current conditions and a short forecast.
No backend: the browser talks to the weather API directly.

overview: A bot for X that watches for a command in replies, analyses the author of the tweet being replied to, and posts a trustworthiness report.
Built around the constraints of a free API tier, which shaped both the polling model and the amount of state it keeps.
highlights: Answers on demand rather than monitoring continuously, which fits inside the rate limits.
Modular command handling, so adding an analysis is a new module rather than a change to the core.
Reports the reasoning alongside the verdict.

overview: A set of computer vision exercises covering hand pose and face mesh tracking, built while learning how the tracking pipelines behave on real input.
Kept because the notes on what fails, and why, are more useful than the demos themselves.
highlights: Hand pose tracking from a live camera feed.
Face mesh detection and landmark extraction.
Frame-by-frame processing with the results drawn back onto the image.

overview: A small scheduled service that keeps free-tier hosts from falling asleep by polling them.
It exists so that a demo link does not cold-start in front of whoever opens it, which is a real cost when the first impression is a loading spinner.
highlights: Scheduled polling on a fixed interval.
Keeps demonstration deployments warm.
Deliberately tiny.

overview: An archive of older creative-coding work, kept because the experiments are still interesting even where the code is not.
It includes fractal trees grown from L-systems, small simulated ecosystems, shader work, and a puzzle built on rule manipulation.
highlights: Fractal generation from L-systems.
Small neural ecosystems where simple agents are given simple drives.
Shader and rendering experiments in the browser.
A puzzle game built around rewriting its own rules.

overview: The first version of this site, kept for reference.
It was replaced by the current build, which is a different thing entirely rather than a restyle.
highlights: The original design and project list.
Kept as a record of where the work started.
